author: PavelMakarchuk
body:
## Diagnosis

### The $7,500 addition (line 2e)

This represents SC's non-conformity to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA). OBBBA reduced federal taxable income by $7,500 via two provisions:

- **$1,500**: OBBBA standard deduction increase (MFJ base from $30,000 to $31,500)
- **$6,000**: OBBBA additional senior deduction for taxpayers 65+

Math check: Pre-OBBBA federal taxable = $108,500 − ($30,000 + $1,600 aged) = **$76,900** = TaxAct line 3 ($69,400 + $7,500) ✓

SC starts from federal taxable income but hasn't conformed to OBBBA, so TaxAct correctly adds back all $7,500.

### Three-way comparison

| Item | PE | TAXSIM | TaxAct (PDF) |
|------|-----|--------|--------------|
| Federal AGI | $108,500 | $108,500 | $108,500 |
| Federal taxable income | $69,400 | $69,400 | $69,400 |
| Federal income tax | $3,451 | $3,451 | $3,451 |
| SC additions (line 2) | $0 | — | **$7,500** |
| SC subtractions (line 4) | $38,290 | — | $38,290 |
| SC taxable income (line 5) | $31,110 | $28,110 | **$38,610** |
| SC tax | $1,166 | $1,044.90 | **$1,677** |

Note: PE vs TAXSIM state tax difference ($1,166 vs $1,044.90) is due to pension allocation — PE assigns all pension to the 65+ spouse while TAXSIM splits 50/50, giving the younger spouse (age 54) an extra $3,000 retirement deduction.

### Fix needed

- **policyengine-us**: SC needs an OBBBA non-conformity addition → PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#7854
